messages.subject: ddply/sample() question
parts:
Hi All,

I have a dataset with multiple dependent effect sizes (r) per row and am
aggregating down to 1 es per study. ddply works great in this case but Im also
interested in reducing another variable (mod2) down to 1 per study.
When aggregating
down to one r, I would like to randomly take one of the values within
the same id (when there
are multiple rows of the same study) and keep the value as is when there is
only 1 row. Below (using sample()) seems to work fine with factors but
not so well with a numeric mode:

id<-c(1,1,1,rep(4:12))
n<-c(10,20,13,22,28,12,12,36,19,12, 15,8)
r<-c(.68,.56,.23,.64,.49,-.04,.49,.33,.58,.18, .6,.21)
mod1<-factor(c(1,2,2, rep(c(1,2,3),3)))
mod2<-c(1,2,15,rep(3,9))
datas<-data.frame(id,n,r,mod1,mod2)

# Factors seem to work as desired

ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
sample(mod1, 1))
ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
sample(mod1, 1))
ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
sample(mod1, 1))


# Numeric seems to behave differently

ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
sample(mod2, 1))
ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
sample(mod2, 1))
ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
sample(mod2, 1))

How can I get this to work as desired? Any help is much appreciated.

AC

messages.subject: Re: ddply/sample() question
parts:
Hi AC,

This is because of an annoying design feature in sample:

replicate(10, sample(10, 1))
replicate(10, sample(c(1,10), 1))

If the first argument is a numeric vector of length 1, then it takes
that as the number of values to sample from. You need something like:

pick_one <- function(x) {
if (length(x) == 1) return(x)
sample(x, 1)
}

ddply(datas, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod = pick_one(mod2))

Hadley

I have a follow-up question for you and the list. However, the q is
tangentially related, so perhaps pointing me to a resource where I can
figure it out would be fine:

Assume this data frame is much larger and I want to repeat this
function, say 100 times, and then derive the mean values of r over
those 100 replications. Is
there an easy way to do this? What about in more complex situations
where the output is r, var(r), wi, etc, and a mean of all output is
desired, e.g.:

cat_sum1 <- function(meta, mod) {
m <- meta
m$mod <- mod
meta <- ddply(m, .(id), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n), mod =
pick_one(mod))
meta$z <- 0.5*log((1 + meta$r)/(1-meta$r))
meta$var.z <- 1/(meta$n-3)
meta$wi <- 1/meta$var.z
return(meta)

OK, the problem is solved. Thanks to Jim Holtman (for final do.call
solution) and Dennis Murphy for figuring this out--petty impressive
work.

cat_sum1 <- function(meta, mod) {
m <- meta
m$mod <- mod

meta <- ddply(m, c("id","mod"), summarize, r = mean(r), n=mean(n))
meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(meta, meta$id), #this code is
responsible for randomly selecting one row (if >1 duplicate id)
function(.data) .data[sample(nrow(.data), 1),]))

meta$z <- 0.5*log((1 + meta$r)/(1-meta$r))
meta$var.z <- 1/(meta$n-3)
meta$wi <- 1/meta$var.z
return(meta)
}

Thanks,

AC
